subject: Post-demo MAP: Technical evaluation milestone, open asks and attachments
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Leah Kim <leah.kim@healthgrid.io>, Tom Brewer <t.brewer@healthgrid.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05 09:12 PDT
Subject: Post-demo MAP: Technical evaluation milestone, open asks and attachments

Hi Leah / Tom — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an explicit MAP milestone for the technical evaluation: what Redwood will run, what HealthGrid needs to provide, and the success criteria we’ll use to qualify moving to Dedicated.

Summary of what we discussed:
- Goal: validate inference latency, throughput, and unit cost across a shortlist of models on your representative prompt set.
- Proposed target close date for this MAP milestone (technical eval complete + acceptance): 2027-05-20.

Technical evaluation plan (proposed):
- Benchmarks to run (Redwood): latency (p50/p95/p99), tail latency for 256/1024 token completions, throughput (tokens/sec at steady state), and cost-per-1M-tokens estimate given batching/kv cache.
- Success criteria (proposed):
  - p95 latency for 256-token completion: < 200 ms (hosted inference, warm KV cache)
  - Steady-state throughput: sustain 8 requests/sec for 256-token median prompt with <= 10% increased p95 latency under load
  - Cost target: <= $40 per 1M input+output tokens (based on current model quantization profile and batching recommendations)
- Model shortlist (initial): Llama2-70B-Chat-q4f16, Mistral-Instruct-70B, Redwood-v0-Chat-63B (quantized). We’ll include smaller 13B fallback variant for latency comparisons.
- Datasets & test harness: we’ll use your 250–500 prompt core set for functional / output quality eval, and a separate synthetic load script for throughput/latency.

What we’re attaching: benchmark template (hg-benchmark-template.xlsx) and a short metrics checklist (redwood-metrics-checklist.pdf) to capture run configs and acceptance results. Please fill the prompt/core-set column in the template and attach the first 50 prompts (sample anonymized) so we can seed the initial run.

Open asks for HealthGrid (action items):
1) Share sample prompt set (first 50 prompts) and one representative long-form document set for context-aware completion tests.
2) Confirm whether the evaluation should run against data in your VPC (private) or using Redwood hosted endpoints (recommended to start). If VPC, we will need firewall/exposed port details.
3) Introduce engineering contact for test-access provisioning (we recommend Tom as discussed).

Ownership & next steps:
- Redwood: Diego (lead) + Ben (solutions) — prepare benchmark harness, run hosted perf passes, and deliver results and recommendations.
- HealthGrid: Leah (procurement/exec sponsor) + Tom (eng) — provide prompt set, grant test access if required, and confirm target acceptance thresholds.
- Proposed kickoff for benchmark runs: 2027-04-09 (30–45 minute technical alignment + verify data access).

If that all looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for the 9th and share the Drive folder where we’ll drop results.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: hg-benchmark-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-metrics-checklist.pdf (doc)

From: Leah Kim <leah.kim@healthgrid.io>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Brewer <t.brewer@healthgrid.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05 13:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-demo MAP: Technical evaluation milestone, open asks and attachments

Hi Diego — thanks for the clear recap, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) We can share an anonymized sample of the prompt set (I’ll attach 50 prompts by EOD). Tom is the right eng contact and I’ve looped him in.
2) Preference is to start with Redwood hosted endpoints to move quickly; we may request a private/VPC run later in the MAP.
3) On success criteria: the latency numbers look reasonable, but can you confirm whether p95 is measured server-side or end-to-end with network + client overhead? We need to know what to compare to our SLA target.

Also, two procurement notes: we have a quick vendor questionnaire (SOC/TLS questions) that procurement will send separately. We’ll need an initial SOW and an estimate of expected monthly spend for the first quarter to expedite approvals.

Leah
VP Product | HealthGrid

On a related note, Tom — any constraints we should call out (eg. IP allowlist windows or data residency)?

--
Tom Brewer <t.brewer@healthgrid.io>
VP Engineering | HealthGrid

[Leah and Tom added in thread header]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Leah Kim <leah.kim@healthgrid.io>, Tom Brewer <t.brewer@healthgrid.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-06 10:27 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-demo MAP: Technical evaluation milestone, open asks and attachments

Thanks Leah — answers inline and updated ownership below.

- p95 measurement: we’ll report both server-side (Redwood runtime) and end-to-end (client+network) numbers. For the MAP acceptance we recommend using server-side p95 as the principal comparison and providing the end-to-end figure for SLA context. We’ll mark both in the results sheet.

- SOW/estimate: attaching a short SOW link in related_links (draft) and including a mid-range cost projection in the metrics checklist. Initial estimate for a 30-day pilot (hosted eval runs + 3 technical consultation hours) is ~$5k–$8k consumption-equivalent (depends on run count and models). We will include a clear line item for dedicated pilot spend if you choose Dedicated afterwards.

Updated responsibilities / timeline: 
- Redwood (Diego + Ben): populate benchmark harness, run the first pass on hosted endpoints (benchmarks + cost calc), and deliver results doc by 2027-04-16.
- HealthGrid (Leah + Tom): supply anonymized 50-prompt sample and long-form context doc by 2027-04-08; confirm whether any IP allowlist/time-window is required.
- Marissa (CC) will schedule the 04/09 30-minute kickoff and owns the meeting invite/agenda.

Dependencies that could affect the target close date (2027-05-20):
- Procurement/signature on the evaluation agreement (DocuSign or PO).
- Test dataset access and any VPC/networking requirements if you ask for private runs.
- If HealthGrid needs an on-prem evaluation we’ll need a longer lead time to coordinate on infra.

Next steps: I’ll drop the populated benchmark template into the shared Drive folder when we get the 50 prompts. Marissa — can you propose 2 time slots for 04/09?

Best,
Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

attachments: redwood-metrics-checklist.pdf (contains cost projection and run mapping)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Hi all — Marissa from Solutions here, jumping in to schedule and make sure owners and deliverables are explicit in the MAP. Proposed kickoff times (pick one):
- 2027-04-09 10:00–10:30 PDT
- 2027-04-09 14:00–14:30 PDT

Deliverable timeline (proposed finalization for MAP milestone):

- 2027-04-09: Kickoff call to verify dataset, run config, and acceptance definitions (Marissa leads agenda).
- 2027-04-12 to 2027-04-15: Redwood runs initial benchmark passes and shares raw results. (Diego/Ben)
- 2027-04-16: Redwood delivers analysis and recommendation (includes model shortlist finalization, quantization profile used, and cost estimate).
- 2027-04-19: Mutual review and acceptance decision window starts.
- 2027-05-20: MAP milestone target close (acceptance or next steps defined).
